record.Subtopic: 水与碳是圈层间迁移的物质主线
record.Section: 3.1 水的特性与地球表面过程；4.1 引言：温室气体与碳
record.Definition / Core Concept: 用同一套 reservoir / flux / timescale 语言开场，并把水循环与碳循环连接到大气、海洋、岩石和生命。
record.Quantitative Information: Ch.3 明确将水分子和碳原子称为表层系统最重要的两种物质；Ch.4 指出 C 是生命圈主干元素。

record.Subtopic: Biogeochemical cycle, reservoir, flux, steady state, multiple timescales
record.Definition / Core Concept: Support transfer of the same analytical language from water to carbon; clarify that steady state can include continuous flux
record.Quantitative Information: Stages may take hours, thousands of years, or millions of years
record.Notes: Source-map ID: M-07

record.Subtopic: Coupled climate components
record.Definition / Core Concept: Climate system includes atmosphere, hydrosphere, cryosphere, lithosphere, biosphere and their interactions; component roles depend on storing and transporting mass and energy.
record.Quantitative Information: None required.
record.Notes: Direct support for a unified Earth-system narrative rather than separate water/carbon lists.

record.Subtopic: Reservoir
record.Section: Flow and Reservoirs; Geochemical Cycles and How They Work
record.Definition / Core Concept: A reservoir is a place/component that stores water or chemicals.
record.Quantitative Information: None.
record.Notes: Use “reservoir” for both water and carbon to support transfer of the framework.

record.Subtopic: Flux
record.Section: Geochemical Cycles and How They Work; The Cycling of Carbon
record.Definition / Core Concept: Flux is flow/transport from one reservoir or Earth-system component to another.
record.Quantitative Information: Figure 12.19 units are Gt C/yr.
record.Notes: Keep storage units and flux units visually distinct.

record.Subtopic: Residence time
record.Definition / Core Concept: Residence time is the average time a quantity of water or a molecule of a chemical spends in a reservoir.
record.Quantitative Information: UE examples for ocean chemicals: sodium ~48 Myr; iron ~100 yr. No numerical global water residence-time table in Ch.17.
record.Notes: Do not present numerical water residence times or the formula storage/flux as UE-derived.

record.Subtopic: 储库、蒸发、降水、水汽输送和径流
record.Definition / Core Concept: 作为水循环主图候选；A 训练识别储库/秒通量，B 训练读年通量与海陆收支。
record.Quantitative Information: A：大气 16、陆地 59,000、海洋 1,400,000（储量单位 10³ km³）；陆地 E 2.2、P 3.5，海洋 E 13.5、P 12.2，河流 1.3（通量单位 10⁶ m³/s）。B：海洋 E 430、P 390，向陆水汽输送 38，陆地 P 109、E 71，径流约 35（单位 1000 km³/a）。
record.Notes: 地球表层的水循环

record.Subtopic: Global overview and pathways
record.Figure Number: W-02, GEOLOGY AT A GLANCE — The Hydrologic Cycle
record.Definition / Core Concept: Core read-the-diagram overview: identify ocean, atmosphere, snow/ice, land, organic, and subsurface reservoirs plus transfers
record.Quantitative Information: Ocean covers 71% of Earth's surface (text on printed p. 581)
record.Notes: Source-map ID: M-02

record.Subtopic: Water as a biogeochemical cycle; cryosphere/ocean transfer
record.Definition / Core Concept: Show living and nonliving reservoirs and explain sea-level response to redistribution between ocean and continental ice
record.Quantitative Information: No required value; source states glacier growth lowers sea level and melting raises it
record.Notes: Source-map ID: M-08

record.Subtopic: Definition and pathways
record.Definition / Core Concept: Water cycles among ocean, atmosphere, land surface and subsurface via evaporation, precipitation, runoff, infiltration, groundwater flow, transpiration, melting, and sublimation.
record.Quantitative Information: Figure 17.2 expresses flows in 10³ km³/yr.
record.Notes: Suitable source for the global overview and Concept Check 1.

record.Subtopic: 水的三相转换与潜热
record.Section: 3.3.2 水的三相转换与气候；3.3.2.1 气态与液态的转换
record.Definition / Core Concept: 说明水循环同时搬运能量；区分熔融潜热与汽化潜热。
record.Quantitative Information: 熔融/冻结约 ±80 Cal；0-100°C 加热/降温约 ±100 Cal；汽化/凝结约 ±540 Cal；1 Cal=4.184 J；正文称气-液相变能量约为固-液相变的 7 倍。
record.Notes: 水在三相转换中的热能传输

record.Subtopic: Humidity, condensation, latent heat
record.Section: 20.3 General Atmospheric Characteristics; 20.6 Weather and Its Causes
record.Figure Number: Fig. 20.5; Figs. 20.18–20.19; captions describe adiabatic cooling, lifting, condensation, and precipitation
record.Definition / Core Concept: Explain that phase changes move energy: evaporation absorbs heat and condensation releases latent heat
record.Quantitative Information: Air cools adiabatically about 6–10°C per km depending on moisture; 14% of atmospheric heat is attributed to condensation in the chapter's energy partition
record.Notes: Source-map ID: M-05

record.Subtopic: Matter states and energy driver
record.Definition / Core Concept: Water shifts among liquid, vapor, and ice; solar energy drives evaporation and atmospheric transport; condensation produces precipitation; snow/ice returns via melting/runoff and sublimation.
record.Quantitative Information: None beyond Figure 17.2 fluxes.
record.Notes: The chapter explicitly links transformations to major fluxes and identifies the Sun as the external heat engine.

record.Subtopic: 植物把水返还大气并耦合碳吸收
record.Definition / Core Concept: 连接 land-vegetation-atmosphere；强调蒸腾与光合作用不是两个互不相干的过程。
record.Quantitative Information: 教材估计全球大陆蒸散把 80%-90% 的水返回大气；一棵大树日蒸腾约 200-1000 L，年吸水约 150 t；全球陆地吸收太阳能约一半用于蒸腾。
record.Notes: 自然产生的气溶胶

record.Subtopic: Climate controls local reservoirs/flows
record.Definition / Core Concept: Local temperature and precipitation strongly control surface and groundwater abundance; cooling moist air leads to condensation/precipitation; mountains create rain shadows.
record.Quantitative Information: Relative humidity example: 50% at 15°C means half saturation capacity.
record.Notes: Keep at process level; global circulation was prior material and should not be re-taught in depth.

record.Subtopic: Water transports sediment/solutes and shapes landscapes
record.Section: F.2–F.3 Shaping the Earth's Surface / Factors Controlling Landscape Development
record.Definition / Core Concept: Support the Part I summary that water moves matter and shapes the surface; water is the dominant global erosional agent among water/ice/wind
record.Quantitative Information: Long-term erosion/deposition rates given as about 0.10–10 mm/yr; not a memorization target
record.Notes: Source-map ID: S-01

record.Subtopic: Partition after precipitation
record.Section: The Hydrologic Cycle; The Hydrology of Runoff
record.Definition / Core Concept: Infiltration enters rock/soil through cracks or pores; runoff is precipitation flowing over land plus near-surface infiltrated water that returns to the surface. Climate controls the partition among evaporation, infiltration, and runoff.
record.Quantitative Information: No global partition beyond Figure 17.2.
record.Notes: Use textbook’s broad runoff definition; avoid treating all infiltrated water as permanently removed from runoff.

record.Subtopic: Lakes/wetlands smooth variability
record.Definition / Core Concept: Lakes, artificial reservoirs and wetlands store high inflows and release water during dry periods, smoothing runoff variability.
record.Quantitative Information: None needed.
record.Notes: “Reservoir” here includes a geomorphic water body; avoid confusing it with only engineered reservoirs.

record.Subtopic: Recharge, storage, discharge
record.Section: The Hydrology of Groundwater; The Groundwater Table; Balancing Recharge and Discharge
record.Definition / Core Concept: Recent precipitation infiltrates to form meteoric groundwater. Recharge is infiltration into a subsurface formation; discharge is groundwater movement to the surface (evaporation, springs, wells, or streams). Balanced recharge/discharge maintains reservoir size and water-table elevation.
record.Quantitative Information: Groundwater 1.05% of all water (Figure 17.1). Chapter text later says ~29% of fresh water (PDF 1675); see conflict.
record.Notes: Keep Slide 15 at recharge–storage–discharge level; porosity, aquifers, wells and cones of depression are not required for the core slide.

record.Subtopic: 冰雪覆盖改变反照率和能量收支
record.Definition / Core Concept: 支撑冰-反照率正反馈的方向链条；用反照率差而非冰期史细节。
record.Quantitative Information: 教材给出海水反照率不足 10%、森林约 10% 或更低、冰雪可达约 80%；低纬与高纬水循环分别表现为气-液和固-液转换的不稳定。
record.Notes: “不同下垫面的反照率差别”；“气候系统两大不稳定区的水循环”

record.Subtopic: Mobile/variable water reservoir
record.Definition / Core Concept: Cryosphere includes ice caps, permafrost and seasonal snow; seasonal and glacial exchanges move water between cryosphere and hydrosphere and affect reflectivity and sea level.
record.Quantitative Information: Ice caps/continental glaciers cover ~10% of land and store ~75% of fresh water; seasonal Arctic/Southern Ocean ice extents and last-glacial sea level (~130 m lower) are given.
record.Notes: The absolute cryosphere volume conflicts with Figure 17.1; use only one dataset.

record.Subtopic: Volatile cycling between surface and interior
record.Section: Controls on Volatiles at the Surface — Cycling of Volatiles Between the Surface and Earth's Interior
record.Definition / Core Concept: Support deep-water/deep-carbon pathway: alteration of ocean crust and sediment stores H₂O/CO₂; subduction returns them to the interior; volcanism returns volatiles toward the surface
record.Quantitative Information: Source estimates roughly half of Earth's H₂O and CO₂ remains in the interior and describes another ocean-volume of water in the solid Earth; use only as supporting context unless primary sources agree
record.Notes: Source-map ID: M-13

record.Subtopic: 水搬运物质、能量与溶质并连接圈层
record.Section: 3.2.2.3 板块运动与水；3.3 地球表层系统的水循环；3.3.2 水的三相转换与气候
record.Definition / Core Concept: 将俯冲/火山、海陆循环、相变能量和生命过程整合成“水连接四圈层”的收束页。
record.Quantitative Information: 本表达把教材分散的储库、通量、潜热与深部交换合并，不引入教材外数值。
record.Notes: 见对应题注

record.Subtopic: Spheres, energy sources, and material cycles
record.Section: 23.1 Introduction / Geology at a Glance: The Earth System
record.Figure Number: GEOLOGY AT A GLANCE — The Earth System
record.Definition / Core Concept: Provide the system frame: lithosphere, hydrosphere, cryosphere, atmosphere, biosphere, linked by material cycles and powered by external/internal energy
record.Quantitative Information: No required memorized values
record.Notes: Source-map ID: M-06

record.Subtopic: Atmosphere evolved through outgassing, ocean condensation, dissolution, weathering, and photosynthesis
record.Figure Number: Fig. 20.2, Stages in the evolution of Earth's atmosphere over time
record.Definition / Core Concept: Compact example of atmosphere–ocean–rock–life coevolution
record.Quantitative Information: Volcanic gas described as 70–90% H₂O with smaller CO₂/SO₂; modern dry air 78% N₂, 21% O₂
record.Notes: Source-map ID: S-02

record.Subtopic: Atmosphere–ocean–rocks–life
record.Section: Components; The Biosphere; Ch.17 introduction and Hydrologic Cycle
record.Definition / Core Concept: Water stores/transports mass and energy, links ocean–atmosphere climate, acts as solvent and geomorphic transport agent, circulates through organisms, and enters soils/rocks.
record.Quantitative Information: <0.1% incoming solar energy used in photosynthesis (context only).
record.Notes: The “moves solutes/shapes surface” claims are supported by Ch.17 introduction, not only the cycle diagram.

record.Subtopic: Heat and material transport
record.Definition / Core Concept: Oceans store far more heat than air and transport heat poleward; continental waters transport water, salt, and organic matter to oceans.
record.Quantitative Information: Ocean liquid water ~1400 million km³; continental liquid hydrosphere ~15 million km³ in this section.
record.Notes: Thermohaline circulation detail is not required for the locked water-cycle sequence.

record.Subtopic: Soil moisture and evaporation
record.Definition / Core Concept: Evaporation consumes energy and cools land; soil moisture, vegetation cover and subsurface water flow influence atmospheric temperature.
record.Quantitative Information: None.
record.Notes: Useful concise coupling example.

record.Subtopic: Water and carbon roles of plants
record.Definition / Core Concept: Vegetation links groundwater to atmospheric moisture and transfers CO₂ to biosphere by photosynthesis; some carbon is buried or precipitated as carbonate shells.
record.Quantitative Information: None essential.
record.Notes: One passage supports the atmosphere–water–life–rock bridge.

record.Subtopic: 温度升高、饱和水汽增多与潜热输送
record.Section: 3.2.1.1 气态水；3.3.2.1 气态与液态的转换
record.Definition / Core Concept: 为 water-vapor feedback 提供物理基础，但“正反馈”定义和最终链条须与指定 UE 来源校准。
record.Quantitative Information: 教材称在当前条件下表面温度每增加 1°C，水汽理论上可增加约 7%；并引用水汽贡献约 75% 温室效应的估计。
record.Notes: “水在三相转换中的热能传输”；“热量的纬向输送”

record.Subtopic: 碳把气候、生命、海洋、沉积物和岩石连接起来
record.Section: 4.1 引言；4.3.5 生命过程与水、碳循环；4.5.1 地质碳储库
record.Definition / Core Concept: 作为 Carbon Part 的开场和总结，并转入两个循环的耦合图。
record.Quantitative Information: 教材直接说明碳循环是氧化-还原过程，生命用光合作用把无机碳转成有机碳；地质作用把碳在岩石圈与表层间交换。
record.Notes: 见对应题注

record.Subtopic: Reservoirs and pathways across air, water, life, sediment, and rock
record.Figure Number: Fig. 23.6, In the carbon cycle, carbon transfers among various reservoirs at or near the Earth's surface...
record.Definition / Core Concept: Supporting synthesis for carbon reservoirs and fast/slow pathways: dissolution, photosynthesis, respiration/decay, weathering, burial, metamorphism, combustion
record.Quantitative Information: Source states about 63 billion tons of C move from atmosphere into life each year; do not use this dated value unless reconciled with UE/CN
record.Notes: Source-map ID: M-09

record.Subtopic: Water, carbon, plate tectonics, weathering, and climate stability form one connected system
record.Section: Chapter overview / The Planetary Volatile Budget
record.Definition / Core Concept: Support the central Earth-system narrative without turning HB into a hydrology source
record.Quantitative Information: No required value
record.Notes: Source-map ID: S-04
record.Evidence Class: SYNTHESIS based on SOURCE-DERIVED HB text

record.Subtopic: Carbon-cycle definition
record.Section: The Carbon Cycle; Geochemical Cycles and How They Work
record.Definition / Core Concept: Carbon cycle is continual carbon movement among Earth-system components; reservoir amounts and inter-reservoir fluxes provide the quantitative system description.
record.Quantitative Information: None at definition level.
record.Notes: Direct bridge from water to the same reservoir–flux language.

record.Subtopic: 表层库与地质库的量级差异
record.Definition / Core Concept: 说明最大储库不等于最快响应，并为慢循环建立数量级直觉。
record.Quantitative Information: 单位 10¹⁸ mol：大气 0.06，生物圈 0.13，水圈 3.3，远洋沉积 1360，大陆边缘沉积 >1370，沉积岩 4250，地幔 27000。
record.Notes: 表层和地质储库中的氧化和还原碳（据 Des Marais，2001 改）

record.Subtopic: Quantitative global carbon cycle
record.Definition / Core Concept: Flux arrows link the major reservoirs; gross exchange can be far larger than long-term net geological flux.
record.Quantitative Information: Terrestrial biosphere–atmosphere 120 Gt C/yr; air–sea 80; dissolved organic carbon/rivers 0.4; carbonate-weathering/formation/sedimentation terms 0.2; silicate-weathering net <0.1; volcanism <0.1.
record.Notes: Do not ask students to memorize all numbers. Do not mislabel the 80 or 120 Gt C/yr gross exchanges as net sinks.

record.Subtopic: 生物、表层海、深海、沉积/变质和地幔的不同“时钟”
record.Section: 4.4.3 碳循环的时间尺度；4.5.1 地质碳储库
record.Definition / Core Concept: 让学生比较系统受到扰动后的快慢响应，不把碳循环看成一条统一速度的箭头。
record.Quantitative Information: 图 4-15：大气-生物圈-表层海约 10¹-10² 年，深层海约 10²-10³ 年，沉积物约 10³-10⁵ 年，地质储库 >10⁵ 年；图 4-16 进一步给出表层库 0-10³、沉积物库 10³-10⁸、变质库 10⁶-10⁹、地幔库 10⁷-10⁹ 年。
record.Notes: “不同时间尺度的碳循环”；“地质和表层碳储库的碳循环”

record.Subtopic: 用相同框架比较水与碳
record.Definition / Core Concept: 把 reservoir-flux-residence time 从水迁移到碳，明确同一语言对应完全不同的尺度范围。
record.Quantitative Information: 所有数值仍按各图原单位呈现，不跨图直接拼接为新预算。
record.Notes: 见对应题注

record.Subtopic: Carbon storage vs flux vs timescale
record.Section: Geochemical Cycles and How They Work; The Cycling of Carbon
record.Definition / Core Concept: Reservoir size and flux rate are distinct; high-flux biological/ocean exchanges contrast with slow geological transfer.
record.Quantitative Information: 120 and 80 Gt C/yr vs <0.1 Gt C/yr for silicate weathering/volcanism; silicate weathering acts over millions of years.
record.Notes: No carbon-reservoir residence-time table is provided; the comparison is qualitative and flux-based.

record.Subtopic: 生物泵、物理泵与碳酸盐泵
record.Section: 4.3.2 表层海的碳汇与碳源；4.3.3 深层海的碳汇与碳源
record.Definition / Core Concept: 区分颗粒/有机碳下沉、溶解态碳随环流下沉、碳酸盐形成与沉积。
record.Quantitative Information: 教材指出深层水无机碳浓度比表层水约高 15%，深海碳循环时间尺度为千年至数万年；图 4-9 为定性路径图。
record.Notes: 海洋吸收大气 CO₂ 的生物泵和物理泵

record.Subtopic: 温度、营养盐、环流对深海储碳的控制
record.Definition / Core Concept: 用一个快慢比较说明物理泵和生物泵对气候扰动的响应不同。
record.Quantitative Information: 冰期-间冰期大气 CO₂ 变化约 90 ppm；教材称南大洋/北太平洋等高纬区是深海水形成和碳泵效率变化的关键区。
record.Notes: “不同温度在大洋生物泵中的不同作用”

record.Subtopic: 溶解碳-生物成壳-碳酸盐-沉积/岩石
record.Section: 4.3.2-4.3.3 表层海与深层海的碳汇与碳源
record.Definition / Core Concept: 显示海洋、生命、沉积物与岩石圈的连续路径，避免进入高级碳酸盐平衡计算。
record.Quantitative Information: 教材给出反应 Ca²⁺ + 2HCO₃⁻ → CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂↑ 说明碳酸盐泵可能释放 CO₂；课堂只用于定性方向。
record.Notes: “海洋吸收大气 CO₂ 的生物泵和物理泵”；“深海 CO₂ 湖的喷口”

record.Subtopic: Liquid water and weathering remove atmospheric CO₂ into carbonates
record.Section: 20.2 The Formation of the Atmosphere; 23.2 The Evolution of the Atmosphere and Oceans
record.Definition / Core Concept: Make the causal connection water + CO₂ + silicate weathering → dissolved/carbonate products → rock storage
record.Quantitative Information: Early-ocean dates are given but are not required for Lecture 16
record.Notes: Source-map ID: M-10

record.Subtopic: Ocean–life–rock connection
record.Definition / Core Concept: Dissolved CO₂ forms carbonic acid/bicarbonate; organisms precipitate CaCO₃; shells settle and burial returns carbon to the lithosphere.
record.Quantitative Information: CaCO₃ weathering/formation/sedimentation terms each ~0.2 Gt C/yr in Figure 12.19 framework.
record.Notes: Avoid advanced carbonate-equilibrium calculations.

record.Subtopic: 含 CO₂ 的水参与硅酸盐/碳酸盐风化并把碳送入海洋
record.Definition / Core Concept: 将水循环明确接入 weathering-carbon transfer，并作为长期负反馈的过程底图。
record.Quantitative Information: 教材列出硅酸盐风化简式 CaSiO₃ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + SiO₂；图 4-16 的风化通量为 45×10¹² mol/a（按原图单位）。
record.Notes: 地质和表层碳储库的碳循环

record.Subtopic: Tectonic uplift exposes rock, increases weathering, and can lower atmospheric CO₂
record.Section: 23.4 Global Climate Change — Long-Term Climate Change
record.Figure Number: Fig. 23.12, Changes in the distribution and elevation of landmasses can affect climate
record.Definition / Core Concept: Connect plate tectonics and weathering to long-term feedback; emphasize conditional language (may, potentially)
record.Quantitative Information: No required value
record.Notes: Source-map ID: S-07

record.Subtopic: Complete source mechanism and figure
record.Figure Number: Fig. 9-10 (deep carbonate/CO₂ cycle); F-01 / Fig. 9-11, Illustration of feedbacks that control atmospheric CO₂ and surface temperature on Earth, as described in the text.
record.Definition / Core Concept: Explain how plate-driven CO₂ input is balanced by temperature/rainfall/acidity-sensitive weathering and carbonate burial
record.Quantitative Information: No single modern budget value is required
record.Notes: Source-map ID: M-14

record.Subtopic: Weathering distinction
record.Definition / Core Concept: CO₂ dissolved in rainwater enables chemical weathering and river transport. Carbonate-rock weathering followed by marine carbonate formation is described as no net atmospheric-carbon change; silicate weathering transfers atmospheric CO₂ into lithospheric carbonate.
record.Quantitative Information: Carbonate-weathering terms ~0.2 Gt C/yr; net silicate-weathering carbon flux <0.1 Gt C/yr.
record.Notes: Critical teaching distinction: do not present all weathering as the same long-term CO₂ sink.

record.Subtopic: 风化、沉积/埋藏、变质、俯冲和火山脱气
record.Section: 4.5.1 地质碳储库；4.5.2 早期地球的碳储库演变
record.Definition / Core Concept: 构建慢碳循环主路径，并与快速生物循环分开。
record.Quantitative Information: 图 4-16 以 10¹² mol/a 表示通量：生物合成 9000、分解 8990、风化 45、沉积有机物约 9、变质还原碳约 2、排气约 2、俯冲约 0.4；图中也标出多级时间尺度。
record.Notes: 见 Seed Figure 核验表

record.Subtopic: 深部碳通过不同构造环境返回大气
record.Section: 4.5.2 早期地球的碳储库演变
record.Definition / Core Concept: 在慢碳循环中区分俯冲输入和火山输出，并提示构造环境控制强度。
record.Quantitative Information: 教材列出的年排碳：大陆边缘俯冲带火山弧约 1.5 亿 t；洋中脊约 0.12-0.6 亿 t；板块内部火山约 0.01-0.3 亿 t。
record.Notes: 冥古宙和显生宙地幔碳循环的比较

record.Subtopic: Geological pathway
record.Definition / Core Concept: UE supports weathering, river transport, carbonate formation, sediment burial, and small volcanic return from geologic reservoirs.
record.Quantitative Information: Sediment burial ~0.2 Gt C/yr; silicate weathering and volcanism each <0.1 Gt C/yr; million-year action stated.
record.Notes: PARTIAL: Ch.12 does not narrate the locked full pathway through subduction and metamorphism, and does not use “volcanic degassing.” Those links need another approved textbook.

record.Subtopic: Ocean circulation transfers heat and can reorganize
record.Figure Number: Fig. 18-14, The conveyor diagram illustrating global movements of ocean currents
record.Definition / Core Concept: Brief system-coupling example only; avoid repeating the Lecture 15 atmosphere–ocean lecture
record.Quantitative Information: Conveyor transport compared with 100 Amazon Rivers; water cools from about 12°C to 2°C in the described North Atlantic branch
record.Notes: Source-map ID: S-06

record.Subtopic: Definition of positive and negative feedback
record.Section: 23.4 Global Climate Change — The Role of Greenhouse Gases
record.Figure Number: Fig. 23.7 is greenhouse-effect context, not the feedback diagram itself
record.Definition / Core Concept: Define negative feedback as slowing/reversing a process and positive feedback as enhancing/amplifying it
record.Quantitative Information: No required values
record.Notes: Source-map ID: M-11

record.Subtopic: Surface temperature depends on insolation, albedo, and greenhouse effect
record.Definition / Core Concept: Give a simple control-system frame before individual feedback examples
record.Quantitative Information: Earth's albedo about 0.3; stated mean surface temperature 15°C; detailed radiative numbers are supporting only
record.Notes: Source-map ID: S-03

record.Subtopic: Positive vs negative
record.Section: Balancing the Climate System Through Feedbacks
record.Definition / Core Concept: Positive feedback enhances/amplifies an initial change; negative feedback reduces/opposes and tends to stabilize it.
record.Quantitative Information: None.
record.Notes: Use the induced-change relationship, not merely “positive = good / negative = bad.”

record.Subtopic: Water-vapor feedback chain
record.Section: 23.4 Global Climate Change — The Role of Greenhouse Gases
record.Definition / Core Concept: Source-grounded chain: warming → more ocean evaporation → more atmospheric H₂O → stronger greenhouse effect → additional warming
record.Quantitative Information: Atmospheric H₂O generally stays less than nine days; this supports fast turnover, not an isolated climate driver
record.Notes: Source-map ID: M-12

record.Subtopic: Water-vapor feedback
record.Section: Balancing the Climate System Through Feedbacks
record.Definition / Core Concept: Warming → evaporation → more atmospheric water vapor → stronger greenhouse effect → further warming.
record.Quantitative Information: None.
record.Notes: Explicitly classified by UE as positive feedback.

record.Subtopic: Why water vapor/CO₂ matter
record.Definition / Core Concept: Greenhouse gases absorb and reradiate infrared energy, including downward, warming the surface relative to a no-greenhouse atmosphere.
record.Quantitative Information: Mean surface ~14°C vs ~−19°C without greenhouse gases; difference 33°C.
record.Notes: Prior context only; do not turn Lecture 16 into a greenhouse-effect lecture.

record.Subtopic: Ice–albedo positive feedback and thermostat interaction
record.Figure Number: Fig. 9-12 is field evidence, not required for the mechanism
record.Definition / Core Concept: Support warming/cooling chain and contrast fast amplification with the slow carbon-weathering recovery pathway
record.Quantitative Information: Snowball scenario states roughly 10 million years of CO₂ accumulation before large greenhouse warming; use only as an order-of-magnitude supporting example
record.Notes: Source-map ID: M-16

record.Subtopic: Ice–albedo feedback
record.Section: Balancing the Climate System Through Feedbacks
record.Definition / Core Concept: Warming → reduced ice/snow → lower albedo → more absorbed energy → further warming.
record.Quantitative Information: Earth albedo ~29% and Moon ~7% in greenhouse context (PDF 1172–1173); these numbers are not required for the loop.
record.Notes: UE calls it “Albedo feedback”; Blueprint title “Ice–Albedo Feedback” is faithful to the stated mechanism.

record.Subtopic: Long response time and negative-feedback direction
record.Definition / Core Concept: Make explicit that warmer/wetter/more acidic conditions increase weathering and CO₂ removal; cooling slows removal and permits volcanic CO₂ to rebuild
record.Quantitative Information: Text gives tectonic timescales of >10^5–10^7 years
record.Notes: Source-map ID: M-15

record.Subtopic: Weathering thermostat
record.Definition / Core Concept: UE supports: silicate weathering removes atmospheric CO₂ into lithospheric carbonate and tends to cool climate over millions of years.
record.Quantitative Information: Net flux <0.1 Gt C/yr; millions of years; Himalayan uplift began ~40 Ma (example).
record.Notes: PARTIAL: term “weathering thermostat” and the causal step “higher temperature/CO₂ → faster weathering” are NOT FOUND in assigned UE chapters. Do not attribute the complete negative-feedback loop to UE alone.

record.Subtopic: Biosphere / plant growth
record.Section: Balancing the Climate System Through Feedbacks
record.Definition / Core Concept: Higher atmospheric CO₂ stimulates plant growth; plants remove CO₂ into organic matter, reducing greenhouse effect.
record.Quantitative Information: No response time or flux is attached to this feedback example.
record.Notes: UE explicitly classifies it as negative. Avoid extending into full Earth-system ecology.

record.Subtopic: Forcing and feedback are not the same; responses span tectonic, orbital, and abrupt-circulation times
record.Section: Chapter overview; Intermediate Term Climate Variations; Summary
record.Definition / Core Concept: Demonstrate that climate responses have different clocks and that fast changes cannot be assigned to the tectonic thermostat
record.Quantitative Information: Intermediate variations 10^4–10^5 yr; abrupt variations 10^1–10^3 yr; weathering thermostat >10^5–10^7 yr from Ch.9
record.Notes: Source-map ID: S-05
record.Evidence Class: SYNTHESIS based on SOURCE-DERIVED HB text

record.Subtopic: Different clocks
record.Section: The Atmosphere; The Cryosphere; The Lithosphere; Carbon Cycle
record.Definition / Core Concept: UE supports relative clocks: atmosphere mobile/rapid; cryosphere seasonal to glacial; volcanic aerosol cooling recovered in ~4 yr; silicate weathering acts over millions of years.
record.Quantitative Information: Seasonal sea ice; last glacial maximum ~20 ka; volcanic recovery ~4 yr; weathering millions of years.
record.Notes: SYNTHESIS/PARTIAL: UE does not provide a unified response-time table for radiative, hydrological, cryosphere, biosphere and weathering feedbacks; plant-growth response time is not stated.
